claim: Abductive and consistency-based diagnosis give the same answers when the model is fully predictive and closure assumptions hold; they diverge only for nondeterministic or abstract models, where abduction under-explains.
agent_test: Run both modes (explain every symptom vs stay consistent) on deterministic simulators and on vague models; expect agreement only on the first.

claim: A diagnosis is a minimal set of parts marked Ab such that the model plus the observations stay consistent; the Ab flag is the unit of hypothesis.
agent_test: Have the agent emit an explicit Ab(part) set plus a predicted-versus-observed table, versus free prose, on fault-injection puzzles at equal tokens.

claim: Finding the best explanation is NP-hard in general; only restricted cases (independent, non-interacting causes) are tractable.
agent_test: Not an agent test; use as a reason to cap hypothesis enumeration and prefer minimal sets.

claim: LLMs can detect that something is wrong or simulate forward far better than they can name the minimal cause: 0.65 vs 0.28 (Elenchos), 96.0 vs 32.1 (TempoBench), any-service 76.0 vs exact set 20.7 (OpenRCA 2.0), DDXPlus 98.7 Hit@3 ranking vs 63.0 generating.
agent_test: Score the same item on detect, simulate and attribute separately; a scaffold should move the attribute number, not only detect.

claim: Selecting among given candidate explanations is much easier than generating them; supplying the right reasoning chain lifts accuracy a lot (True Detective GPT-4 0.38 to 0.83 with golden chain).
agent_test: At equal tokens, compare generate-then-select against free answer; test whether an external hypothesis list helps.

claim: Abduction scores trail deduction across the LLM literature (median 42.50 vs 79.96 pooled; GPT-4 about 42 on syllogism abduction; ART best 68.9 vs human 91.4), but the pooled number mixes unmatched tasks.
agent_test: Run matched abduction and deduction items on our agent to set our own gap.

claim: Models commit to one plausible hypothesis early and stop, leaving budget unused: 86.5 percent of detect-but-misattribute cases had unused probes; cloud RCA agents stop after one cause; anchoring and failure to update predict errors.
agent_test: Add a forced rival-hypothesis step before any stop; measure share of runs that stop with budget left and final accuracy.

claim: Accuracy collapses with the number and interaction of hidden faults: Elenchos exact accuracy 0.32 (k=1), 0.15 (k>=2), 0.03 (interacting pair); OpenRCA 2.0 exact set only 20.7 percent.
agent_test: Build a multi-fault puzzle set; compare single-answer prompt against a minimal-conflict / hitting-set style loop.

claim: Telling the model the fault count trades omissions for hallucinated extras.
agent_test: Vary known-k vs unknown-k with a verification step; check both error types.

claim: Explicit hypothesis-state structure helps: Graph of States (causal graph plus state machine) 39.86 vs best baseline 26.09 human-judged match; ablations 18.12 and 12.32 (LLM judge, full method 31.88); HypoAgent Jaccard 0.885 vs 0.718; LATS-RCA 91.3 vs ReAct 39.8 with 18.9 vs 5.1 hypotheses explored.
agent_test: Compare a notebook of hypotheses with support/refute links against plain chain of thought at matched tokens.

claim: Prompt-only advice does not fix abductive failures: hypothesis-driven and pitfall-aware prompts gave no gain, removing a written procedure did not hurt, agentic loops hurt small models; structure and enforced protocol helped.
agent_test: Test whether a guardrail wording alone changes behaviour versus a code-enforced step.

claim: Right label without grounded evidence is common: correct service named but valid path in 61.5 percent (OpenRCA 2.0); evidence closure 0.38 and 0.15 (Cloud-OpsBench); symptom-as-cause 39.9 percent; diagnosis does not give a valid action (R2Act).
agent_test: Require an evidence chain from predicted behaviour to observed mismatch; audit with a path checker.

claim: Splitting deterministic evidence extraction or scoring from LLM reasoning raises accuracy and cuts cost: EviRCA 40.6-43.9 vs 15.2 with 15-26x fewer tokens; RCAgent compression; ontology scoring; Agentic4PDM host-governed evidence.
agent_test: Move the model-simulation or comparison step into code, keep the LLM for proposing hypotheses; equal tokens.

claim: Free Python matched or beat the richest structured diagnosis tool set (85.4 vs 82.8 top-1), and agents overrode correct tool outputs; more tools are not automatically better.
agent_test: Compare a minimal tool set against a rich one on our agent.

claim: LLM self-critique of its own output damages good answers (11.8 percent regressions) while a deterministic diagnosis with a keep-only-if-error-falls rule cuts that to 1.3 percent.
agent_test: Add a monotone accept rule to revisions: keep a rewrite only if a checker says errors fall.

claim: Hallucinated interpretation of retrieved data is the leading failure: 71.2 percent of runs (Kim), hallucinated root cause in 7 to 40 percent of reports (ORCA-bench), 4 to 40 percent of predictions (Exploring LLM agents).
agent_test: Count unsupported claims per diagnosis with and without a quote-the-evidence rule.

claim: Reuse of past diagnoses helps but unevenly: trajectory-as-ICL JRA 0.76 to 0.83 on one system, mixed on the other; mined rules 14.10 to 35.90 on a held-out cloudbed.
agent_test: Seed the agent with prior solved fault cases; test on same and different systems.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A single gold answer hides underdetermination: 70B-class models give only about 20 percent consistent hypotheses (GEAR); weak models proliferate hypotheses (Cordier).
agent_test: Score a hypothesis set on consistency and diversity, not top-1 only.

claim: Evaluation leakage inflates diagnostic scores: Recall@1 54.3 to 40.3 (Hedges g 0.94); leakage effect exceeded the agent's gain.
agent_test: Use held-out, isolated candidate spaces when evaluating our agent.

claim: An LLM tuned for differential diagnosis beat unassisted clinicians (top-10 59.1 vs 33.6) and improved clinicians' lists (51.7 vs 36.1); one study, curated NEJM cases.
agent_test: Not directly testable; shows ceiling of list-style differentials.

claim: Reasoning-token count tracks human reaction time on abductive items (r 0.552 GPT-OSS-120B; 0.197 DeepSeek-V3), and humans and models fail on the same items.
agent_test: Use token length as a difficulty signal for when to spend extra hypotheses.

claim: Actively choosing evidence is worse than being given it: overall success 0.64 (GPT5.4) to 0.03; order single-turn > passive > active; models fit hypotheses without separating rivals.
agent_test: Give the agent a discriminating-test step (pick the probe that separates two hypotheses) and measure.

claim: Salience capture and presence bias: agents chase the loudest signal and read silence as health (about 24 points AnySvc shortfall).
agent_test: Include silent-fault items; check whether a missing-evidence checklist helps.

claim: ReAct-style tool agents reduce hallucination relative to plain retrieval (4 vs 12 vs 40 percent) but agentic loops can lower accuracy for small models (Llama 3.2 3B 0.31 to 0.23 to 0.05).
agent_test: Compare one-shot, ReAct and plan-execute on our model size at equal tokens.

claim: Simulation-then-compare attribution may be answered by copying visible guards: hiding 75 percent of the transition table drops simulation 79.5 to 31.8 while attribution moves at most 3.4; guard copied on 96.5 percent of steps.
agent_test: Hide part of the model; check whether our agent's attribution truly depends on simulation.

claim: Doing the predict-versus-observe comparison and probe replay in deterministic code gives perfect answers on the easy and additive cases where no tested LLM matched it (Simple Reflex Agent V=1.0 vs LLM exact attribution 0.28).
agent_test: Give the agent a code tool that runs the model and returns a diff; compare with the agent simulating in prose, equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning effort alone does not fix abductive attribution: low to high effort gave no consistent gain and interacting faults stayed at zero at every effort (preliminary, one k=2 set, n=5).
agent_test: Hold token budget fixed, add a forced rival-hypothesis step vs extra thinking budget, on a multi-fault puzzle set.

claim: Prompt-borne domain knowledge (fault-discrimination rules) helps far more than a generic prescribed procedure: Full Score 14.10 to 35.90 with mined rules; removing the five-step procedure raised score in all three conditions (not significant after correction). Rules about discipline did not rescue interacting faults in Elenchos.
agent_test: Compare knowledge cards, procedure text and enforced checks in a matched 3-arm test.

claim: Candidate breadth is the largest component of a tree-search RCA agent (-7.0 points without it), but the search costs 2.1x to 3.8x the tokens and no best-of-N or self-consistency arm was token-matched, so the structure effect is unproven.
agent_test: Add a best-of-N arm with the same token count as the tree method; report both.

claim: In a physical-system test (AUV, 480 trials) the true cause is in the top three for 85-90 percent of frontier trials but ranked first 43-75 percent; small local models fall to 10-78 percent; diagnosis quality and the action decision are not coupled.
agent_test: Score rank-one, top-3 and the action choice separately in every diagnosis test.

claim: A solver or logic layer that verifies LLM-proposed assumptions improves accuracy and robustness over LLM-only reasoning (up to 30 percent relative; 2 percent vs 8.5 percent drop under noise), and sampled-proof aggregation with a small model matched a 120B thinking model with self-consistency.
agent_test: Pair O8 hypotheses with a code-side consistency check before commit.

claim: A prompt-only abduce, act, predict scaffold raises step-level failure attribution 2.4 to 2.9 times over an all-at-once prompt, with the predict step worth 7 to 12 points.
agent_test: Add a predict-then-compare line to the hypothesis record and measure on a held-out fault set.
